key_agent_trends: Open-source agent platforms scale rapidly, with DeepSeek Harness reaching millions of daily users and high token consumption
Consumer assistants accelerate toward proactive, goal-pursuing agents, as Apple pushes Siri in that direction
Agent security consolidates around observability, kill switches, and identity controls for non-human credentials
Coding agents introduce new secret-leak risks via permission shortcuts that store credentials in project files
Cloud-hosted remote agents enable always-on development workflows independent of local machines

stories.headline: DeepSeek Harness AI agent platform reaches 1.54 million daily users and 92 trillion tokens per day
stories.what_happened: DeepSeek disclosed that its open-source agent application Harness reached 1.54 million daily active users on its official API by November 4, less than three months after the August 13 launch. Daily users rose from a 7-day average of about 271,000 at the end of September. Users consume roughly 92 trillion tokens per day, and the platform has about 35,000 third-party plugins, with 60% of active users having created or installed at least one. DeepSeek is preparing an official plugin marketplace and support program for authors.
stories.why_it_matters: Demonstrates rapid adoption of open-source agent infrastructure, highlighting high compute costs of long-running agent workflows and competition with closed labs through ecosystem and price.

stories.headline: Apple accelerates Siri toward proactive agentic behavior, per Bloomberg
stories.what_happened: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple CEO John Ternus is pressuring software chief Craig Federighi to speed up the Siri roadmap. Near-term updates expected with iOS 27.3 include finer control of Apple’s own apps such as Photos and Safari. Broader third-party app integration is targeted for spring. Longer-term, Apple wants Siri to track goals, determine next steps, and pursue objectives without user prompts for every action, similar to OpenAI Dots, Meta Muse, or Grok.
stories.why_it_matters: Signals that major consumer platforms are moving from reactive assistants to autonomous agents that act continuously, raising questions about oversight, permissions, and user control.

stories.headline: Apiiro research: Claude Code 'Don't Ask Again' stores secrets in public GitHub files
stories.what_happened: Security firm Apiiro reported that Claude Code’s 'Yes, and don't ask again' option saves the full approved shell command—including any embedded passwords or keys—into .claude/settings.local.json. Scanning public GitHub found 1,122 of 104,185 copies containing real secrets (1,379 distinct), rising to 2,539 secrets across 1,994 repositories when including history and other files. Types include database passwords, AWS keys, SSH logins, and tokens. Some evaded standard scanners. Anthropic has not publicly detailed a fix.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights a practical security risk in coding agents where convenience features can inadvertently persist and expose credentials in version control.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike launches AI agent Kill Switch and agrees to acquire Fiddler AI and Dreadnode
stories.what_happened: On November 3, 2026, CrowdStrike announced an AI Kill Switch in Falcon Guardian that lets authorized staff terminate a running AI agent, cut its network access, and prevent relaunch. It also signed agreements to acquire Fiddler AI (agent observability and explainability, reportedly ~$400M) and Dreadnode (AI security testing). Deals are expected to close in Q4 FY27; Fiddler technology will become Falcon Observe.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows cybersecurity vendors rapidly adding runtime controls, observability, and pre-deployment testing specifically for autonomous AI agents as enterprise deployments grow.
